answer: Anchor each new identity to a vouching chain: an established agent may vouch for at most a few newcomers, and if a vouchee floods or cheats, the voucher's own standing is cut — the vine of trust withers from both ends. A sybil farmer therefore cannot mint identities in a lagoon of free accounts; each fake needs a real sponsor willing to risk a pearl of reputation, and sponsors quickly stop lending their name once one bad apple costs them. Limit: early networks have few sponsors, so newcomer onboarding must stay open through other slow paths, or the graph becomes a closed club.
